candidates.name: turno-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server wrapping the full Turno (formerly TurnoverBnB) v2 REST API: 49 tools across properties, bookings, blocked dates, projects, assignments, cleaners, checklists, problems, reviews, webhooks. No data committed; single-user stdio mode or multi-user HTTP mode with JWT-embedded credentials. AGPL-3.0, updated 10 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Only a live method for pulling per-property Turno turnover/cleaning-schedule data (a real STR-supply signal), but requires the requester's own paid Turno account credentials — no aggregate/public data accessible. Could theoretically expose booking-adjacent scheduling cadence (a nights/turnover proxy) if the team or a contact already runs Turno for properties, but not a market-wide dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: N/A - live API only, no history

candidates.name: breezeway-python
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client library for the Breezeway.io property-operations API (task management etc.), requires client_id/client_secret. No data committed. MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Method only; Breezeway is a cleaning/maintenance coordination platform for STR operators, but this client needs a paid Breezeway account and returns only that account's properties — not a public dataset.

candidates.name: breezeway (ETL)
candidates.what_it_holds: Automated ETL syncing Breezeway API data (properties with photos, reservations with guest details, tasks, people, supplies, tags) into PostgreSQL for ~2,000 properties, ~3,500 reservations, ~15,000 tasks on average across 8 vacation-rental regions (one operator's private portfolio). No data committed to the repo itself — code/schema only.
candidates.why_useful: Shows the shape of real STR turnover/task data one operator manages (scale: thousands of properties/tasks) but it is a private company's operational pipeline, not a public dataset, and requires their own Breezeway credentials to run.
candidates.geography: unspecified (8 US vacation-rental regions per README)
candidates.size_hint: code/schema only; underlying live data ~2k properties, 3.5k reservations, 15k tasks

candidates.name: breezeway-supply-report
candidates.what_it_holds: Client-side reporting tool that processes Breezeway vacation-rental cleaning exports (likely CSV exports of supply/task data) into reports.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — a report generator over a user's own Breezeway export, not a source of new data.

candidates.name: hostturn-ops
candidates.what_it_holds: Breezeway + Twilio integration for cleaning-ops automation (notifications/scheduling), no data.
candidates.why_useful: Ops automation only, not a data source.

candidates.name: Awesome-Short-Term-Rental-Operations
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated awesome-list of STR turnover/cleaning/maintenance/ops tools: commercial SaaS (Properly, Turno, Operto, Minut, Chekin, Enso Connect, Host Tools) and 4 open-source GitHub projects (tykeal/homeassistant-rental-control, Kamra-PMS/kamra-pms, Gribadan/RentTools.io, lkilpatrick/OpenSTR). No data of its own; a discovery hub. MIT license, 1 star, updated 9 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Useful map of the entire commercial STR-turnover-services landscape (confirms none of the major cleaning/turnover platforms — Turno, Properly, Operto, Minut, Chekin, Breezeway — publish open aggregate data; all are closed SaaS requiring paid per-operator accounts). Good reference if a future scout wants to re-check this space.

candidates.name: homeassistant-rental-control
candidates.what_it_holds: Home Assistant integration that ingests ICS calendars from rental platforms (Airbnb, VRBO, etc.), tracks guest occupancy via a state machine, and auto-generates smart-lock door codes (key-exchange automation) via Keymaster. Test fixtures include sample ICS calendar files; no production data committed.
candidates.why_useful: A generic, reusable method for pulling a given listing's booking calendar (check-in/out dates) as ICS from Airbnb/VRBO — same underlying mechanism as the calendar files Inside Airbnb captures, but per-listing and requires the host's own private ICS URL, so not a route to market-wide data. The key-exchange/door-code angle is a real STR-supply-service touchpoint but generates no dataset.

candidates.name: OpenSTR
candidates.what_it_holds: Self-hosted cleaning-management platform for STR hosts: scheduling, checklists, before/after photo evidence, supply tracking, Airbnb iCal sync, network-aware mobile app. Node/Express + React + Flutter + Postgres. Only demo/seed data (fake properties, rooms, tasks); no real datasets. 3 stars, GPL-3.0, last activity ~Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Open-source alternative to Turno/Properly showing the data model (task/checklist/photo schema) an STR turnover system would use, but ships no real data and each deployment is single-operator.

candidates.name: RentTools.io
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source free property manager for STR hosts: calendar sync across Airbnb/Booking.com/Vrbo/iCal, cleaning-schedule automation, passport-data OCR extraction (Gemini), performance reporting with occupancy/ADR/revenue metrics. Booking data stored in a hosted SQLite instance, not committed to repo. 23 stars, 689 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Notable because it computes occupancy/ADR/revenue reporting across multiple booking platforms per property — again a per-operator tool, not a public dataset, but the most actively maintained (23 stars) of the open-source PMS/turnover tools found.
candidates.last_activity: recent (689 commits, active per repo page)

candidates.name: Kamra PMS
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source hotel/STR property-management system (Frappe framework): front desk, booking engine, billing/tax, housekeeping management, POS, WhatsApp integration, MCP tools for AI-agent-driven bookings/audits. No datasets committed. AGPL-3.0, 34 stars, 18 forks, 352 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Housekeeping/turnover workflow module exists but this is deployment software, not a data source; only relevant if a hotel/STR operator using Kamra agreed to share exports.

notes: This theme is a near-dead end for open DATA: the STR turnover/cleaning-marketplace space (Turno/TurnoverBnB, Breezeway, Properly, Operto, Minut, Chekin, Enso Connect, Host Tools, key-exchange/lockbox vendors, photography-program vendors) is entirely closed commercial SaaS with paid, per-operator, credentialed APIs. Every GitHub repo found is either (a) a thin API client/MCP wrapper requiring the user's own paid account, (b) a private company's internal ETL pipeline (code only, real data never committed), or (c) an open-source alternative PMS that ships only seed/demo data. No committed CSV/Parquet dataset, no release assets, no academic replication package, and no Kaggle/Zenodo pointer surfaced anywhere in this space. Airbnb's own official photographer marketplace and key-exchange partnerships (e.g., KeyNest, Keycafe) also turned up nothing on GitHub beyond generic smart-lock automation tools. Search tooling was a major constraint this run: the shared WebSearch budget was already exhausted (0 queries executed) at the start of my run, and both DuckDB (html/lite) and Bing returned either 403/connection-refused or pages whose extracted markdown had no visible result links (likely JS-rendered SERPs the WebFetch summarizer couldn't parse) — I relied entirely on `gh search repos` (used more than the nominal 4-call allowance because it was the only working channel) plus direct GitHub/raw.githubusercontent.com WebFetch verification, which itself hit a 429 rate limit on github.com/search specifically (not raw file fetches). A future scout on this theme should: (1) request a fresh WebSearch budget or run early before it's exhausted by other scouts, (2) try Google Scholar / OSF / SSRN directly for gig-economy cleaner labor-market papers (e.g. studies of TaskRabbit/Turno-style cleaner marketplaces) rather than GitHub, since any real dataset here is more likely to live in an academic replication package than a repo, and (3) check Airbnb's and Turno's own engineering blogs for any published aggregate stats (headline numbers only, not raw data, but could support a supply-side narrative).
